title: International Economics Adventure 1: Comparative Advantage
welcome_lead: Today you'll see why both countries gain from trade — Ricardo's comparative advantage.
meta_desc: IBDP Economics: David Ricardo's comparative advantage, opportunity cost and gains from trade.
final_note: You computed comparative advantage and showed gains from specialisation and trade.

concepts.def: Focusing on what you do best

walkthroughs.body_html:
David Ricardo's 1817 Principles introduced comparative advantage.

Even if one country is more productive in everything (absolute advantage), both gain when each specialises in goods with the lowest opportunity cost.

UK: 1 hr → 4 wine or 2 cloth. Portugal: 1 hr → 6 wine or 1 cloth.

UK opp cost of wine = 0.5 cloth; Portugal = 0.17 cloth.

Portugal has lower opp cost in wine; UK has lower opp cost in cloth. Specialise and trade → both have more.

Strong assumptions: two countries, two goods, perfect mobility within (none between) countries, constant returns, no transport costs.

Limits: structural unemployment in shrinking sectors, over-dependence on a few exports, environmental costs of shipping.
